finding.claim: Unauthenticated /mirror endpoint fetches a user-supplied URL. The only validation is host.endswith("example.com") with no leading dot (ALLOWED_SUFFIX is defined but unused), so an attacker can register or use any domain such as evilexample.com, or point a DNS record at an internal IP, and make the server request arbitrary hosts, including internal/metadata services. Redirects aren't followed by httpx by default, but the resolved IP is not checked, so a DNS name under an attacker-owned domain ending in example.com resolving to 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1 works. The response length is returned, giving a blind/oracle channel. http scheme is also permitted.

finding.guards_checked: Suffix check on parsed hostname only (bypassable via evilexample.com or attacker-controlled DNS). No scheme allowlist, no resolved-IP validation or pinning, no private/link-local block, no auth on the route. Note: urlparse vs httpx parser differences are a further risk. /ping at line 23 uses a constant URL and is not reportable.
